name: scatter_nicobarese
description: Nicobarese — represented here by Car Nicobarese, the most widely spoken Nicobaric language (Car Nicobar and surrounding islands); written in Roman script. Orthodoxy-classified under the Nicobaric branch of 'Austro-Asiatic', alongside Munda and Khasic; geographically far removed from the subcontinental landmass — the southeastern Indian Ocean island chain. On the standardized 12-column place axis. Voiceless stop pairs across 4 places (bilabial, dental, palatal, velar) plus the glottal stop /ʔ/. Voiced stops at the same 4 places. Four matched nasals (m, n, ɲ, ŋ). NO retroflex stops or retroflex flap. NO voiceless-aspirated stops (so structurally lighter than Khasi). Sibilant /s/, glottal /h/, lateral /l/, trill /r/, glides /w, j/. Inventory drawn from Whitehead (1925) and follow-on Nicobaric descriptions; some sources add voiceless nasal allophones or preaspirated stops in specific dialects (not shown here, to keep the cells phonemic). 19 cells filled.
